Clauses (i) and (ii) are stated in Lean more generally than in the paper: continuity replaces smoothness, support in the closed interval replaces support in the interior, any finite size and arbitrary distinct real exponents are allowed, and the exponential clause imposes no sign condition. Clause (iii) is not. The Lean parametric theorems require a `Family` on an open U whose nonnegativity and support fields hold at every p ∈ U; those are closed conditions, and paper-admissible data on a compact parameter set need not extend. Bridging needs smoothness in p of the moving-support moment integral on a non-open domain, which the repository states only for open U. Both rulings reached OK by assuming that extension step; under the logic-alone rule the verdict is DELTA, relation partial.
